implementation_notes: Swift's structured-concurrency runtime provides the carrier: a static property declared with @TaskLocal holds a value bound for the dynamic scope of withValue { } and inherited by every child task created inside that scope, so a request id or authenticated user can be read anywhere in the task tree without being passed. This replaces the classic context-object-plus-factory structure with a task-scoped binding whose lifetime is the closure; detached tasks do not inherit it, and tasks started with Task { } copy the values in force at creation. The explicit alternative - a request value threaded through Vapor handlers or an actor - stays clearer when only a few functions need the context.
pitfalls: Detached tasks and tasks created before the binding do not inherit task-local values, so long-running background work silently observes nil.
Reading the property outside any withValue scope yields the declared default (usually nil) instead of failing, so a forgotten binding surfaces as an optional-unwrap bug far from the boundary.
